thread.title: Add a Clear button to the session filter, and let Escape clear the query while the filter input has focus.

entries.text:
Add a Clear button to the session filter, and let Escape clear the query while the filter input has focus.

Work in this isolated checkout. Read AGENTS.md first. Keep this change limited to the session filter in src/web/Sessions.tsx and only add styling if the existing styles are not sufficient.

Show the Clear button only when the query is nonempty. Give the search input a clear accessible name. After the button clears the query, keep focus on the search input so the user can type another query. Escape must not clear other controls or interfere with an active IME composition.

Use apply_patch for file edits so the history includes the file diff. Use the existing React and styling conventions. Do not add dependencies or tests that merely inspect JSX. The orchestrator will verify the click and keyboard behavior in a browser with safe <private> sessions.

Run the locked project CLI: ./node_modules/.bin/vp check, ./node_modules/.bin/vp run typecheck, ./node_modules/.bin/vp test run, and ./node_modules/.bin/vp run build. Report unrelated failures without changing unrelated files. Review the diff, stage only this concern, and commit it with a plain conventional commit title. Do not push or open a PR. Do not launch browsers, read credentials, use the live T3 database, or delegate to other agents. Keep the final response short and factual.
I’ll read AGENTS.md, update the session filter, then run the required checks, review the diff, and commit only this change.

description: Launch, smoke-test and stop the toolreader viewer against a safe snapshot of T3's database, then check API responses and the UI. Use when an agent needs to run toolreader locally, verify a change to normalization, the HTTP API or the web UI, or hand a running instance to the developer.

# Test toolreader

Run everything from the repository root. Never point a test run at `~/.t3/userdata/statev2.sqlite` (or `state.sqlite`) with anything but toolreader's read-only open, and never write to it.

## 1. Snapshot the data

Use a snapshot so the run is reproducible and the live database can't be touched:

```bash
rm -rf .t3 && mkdir .t3
node -e "new (require('node:sqlite').DatabaseSync)(process.env.HOME + '/.t3/userdata/statev2.sqlite', { readOnly: true }).exec(\"VACUUM INTO '.t3/statev2.sqlite'\")"
```

Skip this step only when the developer explicitly wants live data. In that case run without `T3_DB`; the server still opens the live database read-only.

## 2. Pick a port and start

Port 4777 is the developer's default and may already be in use. Use another port for test runs:

```bash
lsof -nP -iTCP:4778 -sTCP:LISTEN   # must print nothing
vp build && T3_DB=$PWD/.t3/statev2.sqlite PORT=4778 node src/server/bin.ts serve
```
